narrative.overview:
Axel CRM is a dark-first operational console: charcoal metal, warm cream ink, and a single ember of flame orange for action. It should feel like industrial tooling built for long shifts — precise, durable, and quietly heated — not a pastel SaaS brochure or a cold bank-blue back office.

Density is comfortable-to-dense: operators scan tables, KPIs, and nav for hours. Hierarchy is typographic (Outfit for structure, Inter for data) and structural (left rail, sticky frosted toolbar, content on charcoal). The brand accent is scarce and purposeful; semantic chart colors carry meaning without competing with primary actions.

Default theme is dark. Light theme flips surfaces to warm paper while keeping the same flame primary and type pairing.
keyCharacteristics: Dark charcoal canvas with warm cream ink (not pure white-on-black)
Flame orange (#FC6E20) as the only brand action color
Outfit + Inter pairing; Material Icons Round
Soft lift elevation: hairlines + ambient shadows; hover lift on primary controls and KPI cards
Shared list-page + form-dialog patterns across 20+ modules

rules.name: The One Ember Rule
rules.body: Brand orange appears on primary CTAs, focus, active nav, and sparse accents. It does not fill large backgrounds or entire cards.

rules.name: The Warm Ink Rule
rules.body: On dark, text is cream/parchment — never pure #ffffff for body copy. On light, ink is near-black charcoal, not cool slate-blue grays from the old system.

rules.name: The Blue Is Dead Rule
rules.body: #123499 and blue sidenav fills are retired. New work must not reintroduce them.

rules.name: The Two-Face Rule
rules.body: Structure (titles, nav, KPIs) is Outfit. Data density (tables, fields, long copy) is Inter. Do not invent a third family.

rules.name: The Shell Is Sacred
rules.body: New authenticated screens live inside the shell content region with breadcrumbs — they do not invent alternate app chrome.

rules.name: The Soft Lift Rule
rules.body: Elevation responds to interaction: rest is flat-ish (hairline + low shadow); hover and modal states earn stronger shadows and slight Y translation.

rules.name: The Consistent Corner Rule
rules.body: Prefer the radius scale (8/12/16/20). Do not introduce pill-everything or sharp zero-radius Material defaults that fight the system.

dos: Do use CSS variables (--primary, --ink, --card-bg, etc.) so dark/light themes stay in sync.
Do keep primary CTAs on forge ember and data status on the semantic palette.
Do reuse list-page + form-dialog patterns for new CRUD modules.
Do set headings with Outfit 700 and body/data with Inter.
Do treat dark as the default authority; light is the alternate theme, not a second brand.
donts: Don't reintroduce institutional blue #123499 / #0a2472 sidenavs or primary gradients.
Don't use pure white body text on dark or cool gray Tailwind defaults that ignore cream ink.
Don't flood screens with orange backgrounds — ember is the action accent, not a wash.
Don't invent a third font family or icon set for personality.
Don't copy generic purple SaaS dashboard tropes as brand identity.
Don't invent testimonials, customer logos, or marketing chrome inside the ops shell.
